children: Investment manager GQG Partners loses its bull at UBS on signs of sustained funds-under-management pressure. Lowering his recommendation on the Australia-listed stock to neutral from buy, analyst Fraser Noye tells clients in a note that GQG he sees no clear catalyst for performance or flows to stabilize. He warns that GQG's deteriorating longer-term performance increases risks to fund ratings, client retention and future gross inflows. Noye acknowledges the chief investment officer's strong track record, but worries that sustained pressure could also require greater cost discipline to defend margins and threaten its payout ratio. UBS cuts its target price 73% to 0.49 Australian dollars. Shares are up 12% at A$0.5775. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
